This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-cluster`, touching **34** documentable anchor(s).

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **19** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 73bfe10e75babd8e6bf5f307ad3d77ba84bd6bf8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5173a65284337535c1cefbae27118431b7d4c9f0` — the merge of head `db07746d77c149eb817f75bd291974fd2673d682` into base `73bfe10e75babd8e6bf5f307ad3d77ba84bd6bf8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5173a65284337535c1cefbae27118431b7d4c9f0 && git checkout 5173a65284337535c1cefbae27118431b7d4c9f0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 73bfe10e75babd8e6bf5f307ad3d77ba84bd6bf8 db07746d77c149eb817f75bd291974fd2673d682 && git checkout -B drift-repro 73bfe10e75babd8e6bf5f307ad3d77ba84bd6bf8 && git merge --no-ff db07746d77c149eb817f75bd291974fd2673d682

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 73bfe10e75babd8e6bf5f307ad3d77ba84bd6bf8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 73bfe10e75babd8e6bf5f307ad3d77ba84bd6bf8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `aaf413a4a34dd43404635f2a55235f07104a84c4`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #31932 (body, triage 6740621566, Claim 6740666501, dev report 6741461139), the seat's Step 0 rulings as relayed, PR #31942 body and file list, the net diff against main (5 files, +659 / -0), and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface (the package entry `packages/services/service-cluster/src/index.ts`, the only published subpath besides `./testing`, which is untouched):

- `readClusterMembers(cluster)`: new entry export. **Right**: the ruled reader name, and it takes `{ readonly nodeId: string }`.
- `type ClusterMember` (`nodeId, host, pid, startedAt, lastBeatAt`): new entry export. **Right**: ruled name. The member id is `cluster.nodeId`, as ruled.
- `type ClusterMembership` (`state: 'single-node' | 'live' | 'degraded'`, `self`, `members`, `asOf`, `reason?`): new entry export. **Right**: ruled name and the exact ruled state literals.
- `ClusterServicePluginOptions.membership?: { heartbeatMs?, ttlMs? }`: new optional field, defaults 5000 / 15000. **Right**: matches the ruling. `DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_MS` / `DEFAULT_TTL_MS` are module-private and not exported, as ruled.
- Nothing beyond the ruled names reaches the entry. `ClusterMembershipHeartbeat`, `ClusterMembershipHeartbeatOptions` and `ClusterMembershipLogger` are exported from `cluster-membership.ts` only. `package.json` `exports` has no wildcard or deep subpath, so they cannot be imported from outside. **Right**: the heartbeat class stays off the entry, as ruled. `ClusterServicePlugin` gains only a `private heartbeat` member.
- No spec change: `packages/spec` is untouched, and `IClusterService` / `IKV` are unchanged. No new env var: the only environment reading is the existing `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS` / `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE`, through `declaresMultiReplicaOnRedis`. **Right**.

Store accept set (a cross-replica wire format now, even though it is not on the entry):

- `cluster:member:NODE_ID` holds the member record with a TTL of `ttlMs`. `cluster:members` is a roster with no TTL, changed only by `cas` and only inside `beat()`, which adds its own id and drops ids whose member key is gone. **Right**: matches the ruled keys and the rule that only heartbeats prune.
- The reader accepts only records that pass `isMember`, and roster entries are filtered to strings. A foreign or garbage value is dropped and never trusted. **Right**.
- `Symbol.for('@objectstack/service-cluster:membership')` is a new key in the global symbol registry, set on the cluster instance. It is not a ruled public name. It is an internal handshake that lets the ESM and CJS copies of the module find each other, the same pattern as the existing `:driver-liveness` key, and it does not reach the entry. **Right (internal)**, but see should-fix S1 on its lifetime.

Behaviour the contract states, checked against the code:

- R3: the plugin creates the heartbeat only when `declaresMultiReplicaOnRedis(process.env, this.cluster.driver)` holds. That check runs after `assertClusterDriverSafeForTopology`, so the split-brain guard is untouched. Without the declaration, `readClusterMembers` answers `single-node` with no store I/O. Two CONTROL pins check this (zero KV writes, both undeclared-on-redis and declared-on-nats), and ablation A1 turns them red. **Right**.
- The reader writes nothing: `read()` issues only `get` calls, and the single-node path does no I/O at all. The only state it changes is the in-memory `lastGood`. **Right**.
- Degraded readings: they carry `lastGood.asOf`, not the time of the read (pinned, ablation A8). `reason` goes through `describeConnectionError`, which masks the userinfo of a `scheme://user:pass@` URL (pinned against a password in a URL, ablation A7). With no earlier good reading, the answer is this replica alone. **Right**.
- Logging: a failed beat or a failed shutdown delete logs at `debug` only. No new `warn` line. **Right**: matches the ruling.
- Timers: the beat loop is a chained `setTimeout`. It re-arms only in `.finally` when `!stopped`, it is `unref`'d, and `stop()` sets `stopped`, clears the timer and awaits the in-flight beat. The `withinBound` race timer is also `unref`'d and cleared. No timer is left dangling after shutdown (ablation A4). **Right**.
- Rejections: `beat()` is caught in `tick()`. `read()` catches. The shutdown `delete` has a `.catch` attached before the race. `Promise.all` attaches handlers to every promise, so a second rejection is not unhandled. A start that is not awaited cannot leak a rejection (ablation A9b shows 10 unhandled rejections when the catch is removed). **Right**.
- CAS bounds: the roster loop runs at most `ROSTER_CAS_ATTEMPTS = 3` and stops early once `stopped`. The Redis driver's `cas` is `set` with `ifVersion`: a lost WATCH round re-reads, raises `VersionMismatchError` and returns `undefined`, so each attempt is bounded too. **Right**.
- Shutdown order: `stop()` (which deletes this replica's key) runs before `cluster.close()` on an owned cluster. The delete is bounded to 1 s. **Right**.

Gates (check-runs on the head; their conclusions are the gate verdicts): at 2026-11-09T13:44Z there were 19 success, 15 skipped, 0 failure and 13 still in progress. The 13 running were Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · docs & code guards, and Lint · repo & tooling gates. Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Flag docs affected by code changes and PR-body guards are among the successes. ⛔ This record does not answer the 13 runs still in progress. The seat lands only when they are green. A red one makes this PASS stale and calls for a new record on whatever head fixes it.

Findings:

- **should-fix S1: the membership offer outlives its heartbeat.** `offerMembership` defines the symbol property as `configurable: false`, and `stop()` never withdraws it. This matters for an injected cluster (`ClusterServicePluginOptions.cluster`, `owned = false`, public API) that is reused by a second kernel boot in the same process under the declaration. The second boot's `kernel:ready` handler throws `already runs a membership heartbeat`. `kernel:ready` is a boot-path hook and propagates per `hook-dispatch.ts`, so the boot fails. Also, after shutdown `readClusterMembers` on that instance keeps reading the store through the stopped heartbeat: it does store I/O after shutdown and answers `live` with `self` missing from `members`. The test "one cluster instance runs one heartbeat" pins only the concurrent case. Fix: make the property configurable and delete it in `stop()` (or check `stopped` in `readMembership`), and pin a stop, then start again, on one instance.
- nit N1: under the declaration, a reading taken before `kernel:ready` (no offer yet) answers `single-node`, which the type documents as "no multi-replica declaration". Either document the pre-ready window, or offer the heartbeat at construction and start the beat at ready.
- nit N2: `stop()` awaits the in-flight beat with no bound of its own. Only the delete is bounded to 1 s. With the Redis driver this is capped by `commandTimeout` (2 s per command, and the first failure ends the beat). An injected `IKV` with no timeout can hold shutdown. Putting the `inFlight` await under the same `withinBound` would make the PR body's "1 s bound" true of the whole stop.
- nit N3: `heartbeatMs` / `ttlMs` are not checked for `NaN` or values above 2^31-1. `Math.max(1, NaN)` is `NaN`, and `setTimeout(fn, NaN)` fires after about 1 ms, so a misread option beats Redis in a tight loop. Clamp with `Number.isFinite`.
- nit N4: the TTL is passed as `ttlMs / 1000` seconds, and the Redis driver multiplies it back for `PX` without rounding. A `ttlMs` that is not a whole number of seconds can round-trip to a non-integer, which Redis refuses (unmeasured). The defaults and whole-second values are exact. A `Math.ceil` at either end removes the hazard.
- nit N5: the `lastBeatAt` doc names only the single-node answer as synthesized. The degraded answer with no earlier good reading also synthesizes this replica with `lastBeatAt = asOf`. Name that case on the type too.

### ② Semver level

- The diff publishes a widening only. The entry gains `readClusterMembers`, `ClusterMember` and `ClusterMembership`. `ClusterServicePluginOptions` gains the optional `membership`. No line is removed or narrowed: the net diff has zero `-` lines, and no published accept set is tightened.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` appears in the PR body and in `.changeset/31932-cluster-membership.md`. **Right**: it matches the expected line, and it agrees with the Claim's provisional `yes`.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` appears in both carriers. **Right**: no spec, schema or authorable metadata key changes. The new surface is a runtime reader and a plugin constructor option.
- The changeset grades `'@objectstack/service-cluster': patch`, and it is the only package the diff moves. **Right**: under `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (maintainer ruling A on #25105), the level follows `Metadata-protocol` alone, and `none` grades every introduced entry `patch`. The `yes (widening)` arm does not couple to `minor` for a change outside the protocol. The Check Changeset run on the head is a success.
- There is no `skip-changeset`, and none is needed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1, a membership section in `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx` in round 2: **escalated to the seat.** It is outside the Claim's file surface (`packages/services/service-cluster/src/`, its tests, the root changeset). The seat leans yes. Taking it means amending the Claim's file surface on the card before the dev touches docs. This record does not grant it, and the docs file is not part of what this PASS covers. If round 2 lands docs on this PR, the new head needs its own record. The alternative is a docs follow-up card.
- Open question 2, single-node `lastBeatAt` set to the reading time: **answered, keep (option A)**, in line with the seat's lean. It keeps `ClusterMember` total and the same shape across all three states, and the type documents it. N5 asks for the same note on the degraded answer that has no earlier good reading.
- Dev deviation, the real-Redis three-replica smoke is uncommitted and the committed pins use a shared `MemoryKV` behind a facade named for the Redis driver: **accepted.** The facade exercises the same `IKV` contract and the R3 path, and the ablations show each pin bites. The card's Done-when ("stopping Redis crashes nothing") rests on the smoke recorded in the PR body for the real driver. **Flagged for the seat**: a real-Redis pin belongs in `service-cluster-redis` (which already has `redis-outage.real-redis.test.ts`), so that is a follow-up candidate, not a blocker.
- Dev deviation, ablations A2 and A9 re-run as A2b and A9b: no effect on the contract. **Accepted.**
- Dev deviation, the provisional `Clause-②` was measured as `yes (widening)`: same value with the arm added. **Accepted** (see ②).
- Serial constraint from the Claim, a member id source possibly shared with #31930 (`service.instance.id`): resolved by the ruling, since the id is `cluster.nodeId`. There is no overlap with #31928 or #31931 in this diff's files. **Answered.**
- Security: `reason` and the debug lines carry only redacted text. The stored record holds the hostname and pid, and no credential. No other boundary flags were raised. **None open.**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `db07746d77c149eb817f75bd291974fd2673d682`
Local-runs: none

This is a delta review against the record on `aaf413a4`, and it is a whole record for this head. It replaces that record. Inputs read:
- the delta `git diff aaf413a4 pr-31942` (3 files, +145 / -13);
- the net diff against main (6 files, +792 / -1; the one `-` line is in `cluster.mdx` prose);
- the updated PR body;
- card #31932's claim amendment 6741506464 (no newer card comment);
- the check-runs on this head.

The tier still holds. The new path `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx` is not schema: the suspect glob is `packages/spec/src/**`. It is not a governed-register row either (`docs/adr/`, `.claude/`, `skills/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, workflows). So the review is still owed only by the `Clause-②: yes` declaration. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface: no change since `aaf413a4`. Neither `index.ts` nor `cluster-service-plugin.ts` is in the delta.
- The entry still gains exactly the ruled names: `readClusterMembers`, `ClusterMember` and `ClusterMembership`, with states `'single-node' | 'live' | 'degraded'`.
- `ClusterServicePluginOptions` gains `membership?: { heartbeatMs?, ttlMs? }`, with defaults 5000 / 15000 and the constants not exported.
- `ClusterMembershipHeartbeat`, its options and its logger type stay off the entry, and `package.json` `exports` has no other path to them.
- There is no spec change and no new env var.

**Right**, as before.

Accept-set and behaviour changes in the delta:

- **Offer lifetime (S1 → resolved).**
  - `offerMembership` now defines the property with `configurable: true`.
  - `stop()` calls `withdrawMembership` synchronously, before clearing the timer. That deletes the key only if it still points at this heartbeat, so a stop called before `start()`, or a stale heartbeat, cannot pull off someone else's offer.
  - After shutdown, `readClusterMembers` answers `single-node` with no store I/O. A second kernel on the same injected cluster boots, because the `hasOwnProperty` refusal now sees no property.
  - The concurrent double-start refusal is kept: the "one cluster instance runs one heartbeat" pin is unchanged.
  - The new pin "a cluster instance handed to a second kernel" checks `single-node` between the two boots, that `bootstrap()` resolves, and `live` afterwards. Ablations S1a and S1b on the PR body each turn it red.
  
  **Right.**
- **Timing guard (N3 → resolved for NaN, Infinity and ≤ 0; residue kept as nit N3′).** `positiveOr` sends any value that is not a finite positive number to the default, for both options. `ttlMs` is still at least two beats. The NaN pin (2 writes in 150 ms) is red under ablation N3. **Right.** Two cases still pass the guard:
  - a finite value above 2^31-1, which `setTimeout` clamps to 1 ms;
  - a value in (0, 1), which `setTimeout` also runs at about 1 ms.
  
  This is not a contract break: no ruling and no option documentation promises these.
- **Whole-second TTL (N4 → resolved).**
  - The member key is written with `ttl: Math.ceil(ttlMs / 1000)`, so the Redis driver's `* 1000` into `PX` is always an integer.
  - The effective TTL can now be up to 999 ms longer than `ttlMs`. The option docblock and §8.2 say so ("rounded up to whole seconds"). The changeset's "drops out within the TTL" stays true of the stored TTL.
  - The TTL pin (1500 → `ttl: 2`) is red under ablation N4.
  
  **Right.**
- **Pre-ready and post-shutdown `single-node` (N1 → resolved by documentation).**
  - The `ClusterMembership.state` docblock, the `readClusterMembers` docblock and the §8.2 table now name the window: a declared deployment reads `single-node` before `kernel:ready` and after shutdown.
  - The behaviour is unchanged, and it is now what the type says.
  
  **Right.**
- **`lastBeatAt` synthesis (N5 → resolved).** The `ClusterMember.lastBeatAt` docblock and the §8.2 table now name both synthesized cases: the single-node answer, and a degraded answer with no earlier good reading. **Right.**
- **Shutdown in-flight bound (N2 → not addressed; carried as nit).** `stop()` still awaits the in-flight beat without its own limit. With the Redis driver, the 2 s `commandTimeout` caps it, and the first failed command ends the beat. The PR body's wording ("waits for an in-flight beat, deletes its own member key within a 1 s bound") is accurate about which part is bounded. This is not a contract break.

Hazards re-checked on this head; none reopened:
- The beat loop still re-arms only when `!stopped`, it is `unref`'d, and `stop()` clears the timer. No timer outlives shutdown.
- `beat()`, `read()` and the shutdown `delete` all keep their catches. No unhandled rejection is possible.
- The reader only `get`s, so it writes nothing.
- The R3 guard in the plugin is untouched. The CONTROL pins and ablation A1 are unchanged.
- The roster CAS loop is still bounded at 3 attempts and by `stopped`.
- `reason` and both debug lines still go through `describeConnectionError`.

Docs, `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`:
- §8.2 Membership is new, and one sentence in §8 now points to it. It sits under "8. Configuration surface", after §8.1. Everything it states matches the code:
  - the declaration gate;
  - the key names;
  - CAS-only, heartbeat-only roster pruning;
  - the member id is `cluster.nodeId`, random per process unless config sets `nodeId` (as `defineCluster` shows);
  - the defaults;
  - the whole-second rounding;
  - that the spec's `heartbeatMs` is not read;
  - the three-state table with the degraded `asOf`;
  - `reason` present only on degraded and credential-free;
  - debug-only logging.
- "Neither the boot nor any request waits on a beat" is true, because only shutdown waits (N2).
- `content/docs/references/` is untouched: the `git diff --stat` of that tree is empty. The section matches what the amendment allows. **Right.**

Tests, `cluster-membership.test.ts`:
- The only edits to existing lines are `HEARTBEAT_MS` 40 → 100 and `TTL_MS` 160 → 1000. Everything else is new code. The change is forced by N4: a 160 ms TTL now rounds up to 1 s, and the kill pin's ceiling `TTL_MS + HEARTBEAT_MS * 2` would otherwise be shorter than the real expiry.
- No assertion changed. Every wait is still written in beats or TTLs, never in fixed milliseconds:
  - the shutdown pin still waits 5 beats for zero writes;
  - the CONTROL pins still wait 4 beats for zero writes;
  - the outage pin still waits 3 beats;
  - the kill pin keeps TTL plus 2 beats. That margin is now 20 % of the TTL instead of 50 %, so the pin is tighter, not looser.
- The pins are **not weakened**.
- Three pins are added: second kernel, whole-second TTL, and NaN default. The total is 11.

Gates (check-runs on the head; their conclusions are the gate verdicts): at 2026-11-09T14:19Z there were 39 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure and 1 in progress.
- The run still in progress is a second `Check Changeset` run; a `Check Changeset` run on this head has already succeeded.
- Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check, all Lint jobs (ESLint and docs & code guards included), Build Docs and Flag docs affected by code changes are among the successes.

⛔ This record does not answer the run still in progress. The seat lands only when it is green.

Findings on this head:
- No must-fix and no should-fix.
- **nit N2 (carried):** bound the `await this.inFlight` in `stop()` with the same `withinBound`.
- **nit N3′ (residue of N3):** `positiveOr` accepts values above 2^31-1 and values in (0, 1), and `setTimeout` runs both at about 1 ms. Add an upper clamp, or keep the old `Math.max(1, …)` floor alongside the finiteness check.
- **nit N6 (new, cosmetic):** one line in the new §8.2 runs to about 130 columns ("never below two beats, and the store receives it rounded up to whole seconds. The spec field `heartbeatMs` on the cluster"), unlike the wrapped prose around it. A small slip in the PR body: Acceptance notes says the smoke is "below", but it is above.

### ② Semver level

- The delta changes no published surface. It only changes behaviour for out-of-domain option values, which used to produce a broken loop, and the rounding of the stored TTL. The net diff still publishes a widening only: three new entry exports and one optional plugin option, with no narrowed accept set.
